sentences.text: Neuquenornis lived during the Santonian age, approximately 85 to 83 million years ago, with a more restricted time range of 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
Informal estimates place the bird's length at nearly 30 centimeters, while the holotype fossil indicates a length of 23.5 centimeters, a hip height of 17 centimeters, and a weight of 205 grams.
This small creature possessed long legs and a tarsometatarsus measuring 46.8 millimeters in length, featuring hooked claws adapted for perching and foraging on the ground or in shallow water.
Evidence suggests Neuquenornis lived in nesting colonies and buried its eggs in a behavior similar to megapodes.

The species was formally described by Chiappe and Calvo in 1994, based on the holotype specimen cataloged as MUCPv-142, which is housed in the collection of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales at the Universidad Nacional del Comahue in Neuquen, Argentina.
Chiappe and Calvo originally classified Neuquenornis in the family Avisauridae within the Enantiornithiformes.
Fossils were found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, which dates to the Santonian stage between 85 and 83 million years ago.
Recent unpublished analyses suggest Neuquenornis may be more closely related to Concornis and Cathayornis than previously thought.
